claims.text: The initial HfNbTaTiZr alloy is homogeneous and single-phase.
Temperature-dependent short-range ordering governs the stress–strain behavior of HfNbTaTiZr.
Local compositional clustering governs the thermoelastic behavior of HfNbTaTiZr.
Thermal aging in the 600–800 °C range promotes short-range ordering.
Rapid quenching suppresses ordering and freezes a relatively disordered state.
The comparison will use samples with identical initial processing and will vary their subsequent thermal history.
TEM or atom-probe tomography can quantify the evolution and extent of short-range ordering or local compositional clustering in the samples.
Thermally activated short-range ordering or clustering alters dislocation interactions.
Short-range ordering or clustering creates local regions with different stiffnesses.
Short-range ordering or clustering creates local regions with different thermal-expansion coefficients.
Promoted short-range ordering increases resistance to high-temperature creep.
At the same load and 1250 °C, aged samples with promoted short-range ordering will have a lower creep strain rate than rapidly quenched samples.
Promoted short-range ordering increases cold-work and aging-induced hardening.
Aged samples with promoted short-range ordering will exhibit greater microhardness after cold work and aging than rapidly quenched samples.
Promoted short-range ordering modifies elastic modulus between 293 and 1100 K relative to the rapidly quenched baseline.
Promoted short-range ordering modifies the magnitude or temperature dependence of thermal expansion between 293 and 1100 K relative to the rapidly quenched baseline.
The influence of short-range ordering is expected to be relevant from 293 K through 1250 °C.
Precipitation may provide an alternative explanation and cannot be excluded without microstructural analysis.
